A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ICQF research. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–I support reliable comparison, including matching content across pagination changes and the additional figure in v4.

before.justification: v3 reports original synthetic latent-dimension recovery experiments and empirical CBCL analyses on HBN and ABCD, including diagnostic prediction and factor-loading stability results.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experimental results and adds an ℓ1-NMF factor-loading result to the qualitative CBCL-HBN comparison.

M1.justification: The underlying bounded ICQF method, confound handling, and optimization updates are retained. v4 explicitly includes loading upper bounds in the optimization equation, but v3 already required loadings to stay within questionnaire response ranges; this does not establish a new procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic questionnaire scenarios, CBCL data from HBN and ABCD, and questionnaire coverage in Appendix F. The added ℓ1-NMF analysis uses the existing CBCL-HBN qualitative setting.

E2.justification: Section 4.2.3 and Appendix H add ℓ1-NMF to the qualitative loading comparison previously conducted between ICQF and FA-promax. ℓ1-NMF already participated in quantitative experiments, whose comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4 revises the blanket common β=0.1 setting: v4 restricts it to untuned experiments and specifies joint BCV selection of k and β for each method when tuning. v3 already reports some tuning, so this is a reported protocol revision without evidence that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The qualitative case study now examines whether ℓ1-NMF produces interpretable loading patterns, supported by its added heatmap in Appendix H. Existing noise-level comparisons, sample-size analyses, cross-study stability tests, and clinical assessments in Appendix I are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report 30 generated synthetic datasets, 30 seeded clinical dataset splits, the same standard-error and standard-deviation practices, 95% confidence regions, and Wilcoxon tests with false-discovery-rate adjustment. No new uncertainty procedure accompanies the added qualitative comparison.

E6.justification: v4 newly reports the qualitative ℓ1-NMF solution with BCV-selected β=0.0 and k=11, including its loading heatmap and the observation that a few large-magnitude factors dominate the display. Existing numerical results in Tables 1–4 and diagnostic AUC curves in Figure 3 are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 changes the formal loading feasible set from Qij≥0 to 0≤Qij≤bj and defines item-specific response bounds, with an entry-specific generalization in a footnote. This completes the mathematical specification of previously described bounds. Propositions 3.1–3.2 and their proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction replaces local-minimum convergence wording with KKT-point convergence under ρ≥√2 and conditions its near-global statement on correctly specified dimensionality. The abstract explicitly attributes interpretability assessment to clinical collaborators and co-authors. Central empirical claims remain unchanged, while stronger convergence wording persists in the discussion.

C2.justification: v4 explicitly states that box constraints do not ensure uniqueness or full identifiability and that γ does not remove scale ambiguity. It adds explanations of symptom-group splitting and additive latent factors, and interprets the new ℓ1-NMF result as showing possible misalignment between reconstruction-based tuning and interpretability.

D1.justification: v4 specifies that all 200 synthetic samples are used for dimension recovery and that held-out ICQF scores are obtained by optimizing W while fixing trained Q. These add detail to existing experiments. Code access, optimization pseudocode, runtime description, and the appendix setting ρ=3 remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The introduction newly frames ICQF as unifying established tools and locates its technical contribution in clinically motivated constraints and associated guarantees. This is a limited positioning refinement; Section 2 and the cited-work set are unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 makes localized rewrites and explanatory additions in the abstract, introduction, methods, and experimental descriptions, and updates author order and contact information. The overall section sequence and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Appendix H adds Figure 6, combining retained ICQF and FA heatmaps with a new ℓ1-NMF panel; the earlier enlarged comparison remains. Subsequent figures are renumbered, Figure 2's caption is shortened, and content placement shifts. Existing plots and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v4 improves assessability through clearer bounds, tuning and inference descriptions, explicit identifiability limitations, and an additional qualitative baseline comparison in Section 4.2.3 and Appendix H. These are useful, limited gains. Existing empirical results and proofs are unchanged, and the discussion retains stronger convergence language despite the introduction's qualification.
